title: Consolidated callpath sparse-sketch warehouse curation for compact console analytics
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Curate a compact, query-friendly table set that encodes invocation callpaths and session-level summaries using sparse sketches and deduplicated call lineage. This will power Console real-time charts, per-route cost allocation, and drilldowns without requiring expensive multi-join queries across raw callstream events.
background: Current Console tooling aggregates from the raw callstream and several denormalized marts which results in heavy join patterns for common queries (per-tenant cost by route, session tail-latency slices, and callpath frequency heatmaps). Those queries are expensive and slow for interactive Console dashboards and ad-hoc exploration. We want a consolidated curated layer that encodes session callpaths as compact signatures plus lightweight aggregated metrics to make Console UI queries fast and bounded in cost.
acceptance_criteria: A single consolidated table (callpath_summaries) contains one row per invocation-session-shingle keyed by tenant_id, session_id, shingle_start_ts and callpath_signature
Query patterns for Console Overview and Route Drilldown return within 1s for 90% of requests (95th < 3s) for typical time windows (7d/30d) when run against the curated tables
End-to-end backfill for last 90 days completes within the non-peak 48-hour migration window
Storage overhead is <= 20% compared to existing denormalized marts while reducing typical join counts by >= 3x
Cost attribution queries (per-route token/cost rollups) match existing golden queries within 1% discrepancy (documented tolerance)
Automated unit and integration tests for signature generation, shingle windowing, and dedup logic are present in the PR
technical_notes: Callpath signature: generate a deterministic 64-bit fingerprint by hashing the ordered list of route IDs (FNV64 then irreducible mixing). This trades off perfect invertibility for compactness. We will also store a sample_proto_callpath column (string) containing the most frequent expanded route path per signature for tooling and rare-case audits.

Shingle window: 30s session shingle with sliding 10s stride to capture short-lived multipath invocations. Each shingle row aggregates token counts, producer latency histograms (approx quantile sketch), and error counters.

Sparse sketches: use HyperLogLog++ for unique route cardinality inside the shingle and t-digest for latency quantiles. Implement sketch serialization in column-friendly binary format (base64 in JSON exports) for downstream UDFs.

Dedup and de-noise: use tenant-scoped dedup bloom filter during streaming ingestion to avoid double counting retries within the shingle window. The bloom filter state is periodically checkpointed and compacted in nearline processing.

Storage layout: partition by day (event_date) and cluster by (tenant_id, callpath_signature) to optimize typical Console scans. Use compaction policy to merge small files hourly for low-latency reads.
Materialized views: expose pre-aggregated per-tenant/per-route daily rollups (callpath_daily_rollup) and a compact top-k signatures table (callpath_topk) refreshed via incremental job every hour.
Backwards compatibility: keep existing denorm marts untouched during rollout; provide a mapping table (callpath_signature -> legacy_route_set) to aid gradual migrations of dashboards and alerts.
Query examples: provide sample SQL for Console backend endpoints (overview, route detail, top callpaths) optimized to hit the curated tables directly with LIMIT and time-bounded filters.
Privacy: ensure removal of any PII; signatures and samples are sanitized and sampled at tenant-level. Add a per-tenant opt-out flag for storing expanded callpath samples.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (PoC): implement signature generator and shingle aggregator in a test streaming job; produce nightly sample output for a single internal tenant and run comparative queries
Phase 2 (Pilot): run hourly incremental pipeline for 10% of production tenants; create callpath_topk materialized view and compare Console latency/cost against baseline
Phase 3 (Backfill): execute backfill job for last 90 days into callpath_summaries with resource throttle; monitor job progress and re-run failed partitions; validate cost attribution tolerance
Phase 4 (Swap): update Console API to prefer curated tables for read paths behind a feature flag; run parallel canary traffic and compare metrics before full cutover
Phase 5 (Decommission): once stable for 14 days and no regressions, deprecate the old join-heavy denorm queries and remove the temporary mapping table

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hash collisions could merge semantically different callpaths. Mitigation: use 64-bit mix + store sample_proto_callpath to detect/resolve frequent collisions; run collision detector during backfill.
Risk: Backfill may spike cost. Mitigation: run backfill during non-peak, throttle concurrency, and use incremental checkpoints so failed partitions can resume without full restart.
Risk: Query regressions for edge dashboards. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout with canary traffic and comparison dashboards; fallback to old denorm queries if regressions observed.
Risk: Increased storage from sketches. Mitigation: tune sketch precision parameters to balance size/accuracy and provide retention policy for >90d raw sketches (archive to cold storage).
